Amy Poehler's Peacock Comedy 'Dig' Adds Jason Mantzoukas, Max Greenfield and Four More to Cast

New Cast Members Join Amy Poehler's 'Dig'

Peacock's upcoming comedy series "Dig," starring Amy Poehler, has added five actors to its ensemble, according to reporting by Variety. Jason Mantzoukas, Brennan Lee Mulligan and Noma Dumezweni will recur, while Max Greenfield and Dan Bucatinsky will guest star.

Characters and Premise

Based on Kate Myers' book "Excavations," "Dig" follows a team of dedicated archaeologists—and less-dedicated college students—who spend their summer working on a dig site in Greece. Per the streamer's logline, their discovery of a rare artifact sends them on the adventure of a lifetime.

Character descriptions provided by Peacock and shared in the report include:

  • Jason Mantzoukas plays Lambros, a local store owner and occasional looter of treasures unearthed at the dig site.
  • Brennan Lee Mulligan plays Marcus Robertson Jr. ("M.R."), a wealthy dilettante deciding whether to donate money to support the dig.
  • Noma Dumezweni plays Evelyn, the mother of Clare (Antonia Thomas), who looms large in Clare's life and weighs in on her decisions.
  • Max Greenfield plays Andrew, a high-society art dealer whom Poehler's character, Elise, meets at a fancy party.
  • Dan Bucatinsky plays Fritz, a New York museum director who takes an interest in Clare's career.

Poehler leads the cast, which also features Hugh Laurie, Geraldine Viswanathan, Antonia Thomas and Fina Strazza.

Creative Team and Release

Poehler co-created "Dig" with Michael Schur, her former "Parks and Recreation" boss. Schur also co-created "Brooklyn Nine-Nine" and was a major creative force behind the American version of "The Office." J.J. Philbin also serves as a writer on the series.

Executive producers include Morgan Sackett, Dean Holland, Kate Arend, Jordan Grief, Dave Becky, David Miner, Sharon Jackson and author Kate Myers. The series is produced by Universal Television, a division of Universal Studio Group, along with Fremulon, Paper Kite, Duck Duck Films, Dunshire, 3 Arts and Ocean Avenue.

All episodes are scheduled to premiere on Peacock on Nov. 23.

What Is Confirmed, What Is Unknown, and How to Verify

Confirmed details in this report—the casting additions, character descriptions, premiere date, co-creators, executive producers and production companies—come from the trade publication's reporting.

Not addressed in the source are the total episode count for the first season, whether further casting announcements are expected, or specific plot developments beyond the published logline. The report also does not indicate how many episodes each new actor will appear in.

Readers can review the original announcement and reporting at Variety: https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/amy-poehler-dig-max-greenfield-jason-mantzoukas-1236910704/

Practical Implications and Comparisons

For audiences, the new additions suggest an ensemble built around Poehler's Elise, with story threads reaching into local commerce, wealthy patronage, family relationships and the art and museum worlds. Michael Schur's involvement invites comparison to his earlier workplace comedies, though the source material—an archaeological dig in Greece—points to a setting and premise distinct from the office-based humor of "Parks and Recreation" or "Brooklyn Nine-Nine." The plan to release all episodes at once on Peacock also places "Dig" within the streamer's binge-release model rather than a weekly rollout.
